repositories.evidence: Origin separately: the supplied response-record rename makes address GETs emit postcode; AddressRequest and controller request handling retain postalCode.

AccountClient binds the GET body to a postalCode component and passes it to CheckoutService, which sends it to ShipmentClient. With only postcode supplied, normal quote creation cannot preserve the postal code; ShipmentClient's Map.of request body rejects a null value before its HTTP call.
The Order client retains the original postalCode request field, but Shipment server execution is outside the bounded check.

obligations.evidence: Validate GET responses use postcode while create/update request bodies still use postalCode.
Repair the Account GET response read mapping to consume postcode while retaining Order's internal and Shipment-request postalCode naming.
Validate the repaired Order quote flow still submits postalCode to the estimate boundary; no Shipment production edit follows from this change.

edges.evidence: Account exposes the GET route and Order's AccountClient requests that path and reads postalCode.
Checkout passes the address postalCode to ShipmentClient, whose request body uses postalCode.

actions.evidence: Map the provider's new response field postcode into the existing Order postal-code value used by CheckoutService and ShipmentClient.

limitations: Shipment server behavior, provider routing/security, persistence, UI, and Kafka execution (including later order-confirmed processing) were excluded from this bounded check.
additional_recommendations: Update Account GET-response contract tests from postalCode to postcode, and add an Order integration test that reads postcode from Account while asserting the estimate request still contains postalCode.
